A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including the complete main text, references, and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original transfer-learning experiments and measured correlations comparing transferability estimators, with results in Section 4, Tables 1–2 and 4–9, and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the transferability comparisons, runtime measurements, and k-NN sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: The k-NN estimator is identical: an 80%/20% target-training split, cosine similarity between extracted features, default k = 200, and classification accuracy as the transferability score. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same source and downstream datasets, DomainNet domain-shift scenarios, and class-count variation tasks on NABirds, SUN397, and Caltech-256. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including the transferability metrics, domain-distance metrics, and mean-dist aggregate. The scenario-specific omissions of inapplicable comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 2–4 and Appendix A retain identical splits, preprocessing, training settings, architecture configurations, and testing procedures. Absolute and relative performance definitions, weighted Kendall correlation, and the alternative evaluation measures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The factor-isolation studies and appendix analyses are retained unchanged: metric intercorrelations, task-complexity trends, runtime comparisons, sensitivity to k, and alternative evaluation measures in Figures 7–13.

E5.justification: The three-fold cross-validation statement in Section 2 and statistical reporting throughout the results and appendices are identical. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Tables 4 and 5 report the same average k-NN weighted Kendall correlations of 0.60 for absolute performance and 0.90 for relative performance under joint domain/task changes.

T1.justification: The definitions and formulas for relative transfer performance, its predicted counterpart, and transfer gap in Section 3 are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about existing metrics' inconsistent reliability and k-NN's effectiveness, efficiency, and simplicity. The scope and claimed contributions are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same interpretation of k-NN as a feature-separability proxy for fine-tuning and the same explanations of other metrics' weaknesses. No applicability boundary, failure condition, or substantive limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures are identical, including preprocessing, optimizers, learning rates, the 1,000-iteration warm-up, and validation-based checkpoint selection. Dataset details, computing-resource acknowledgments, and access information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography match, as do the Related work and Contributions w.r.t previous works passages. There is no change in novelty claims or positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds Emir Konuk to the author list, removes the running-title text, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page author line is adjusted and the running title is removed from subsequent pages. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–9 retain the same appearance, captions, structure, and placement; the layout changes are limited to page furniture.

improvement.justification: v2 changes authorship and running headers while retaining the scientific text, results, appendix analyses, and reproducibility details unchanged. These limited edits establish no meaningful net difference in the paper's scientific quality or clarity.
